item.title: Small and very scary: Rare miniature T.rex dinosaur skeleton fetches €42 million at auction
item.description: A dinosaur that looks like a tiny Tyrannosaurus rex is now one of the world's most expensive fossils having been sold at a Sotheby's auction for €42.6 million in New York.

item.title: Has the White House tipped rapper Nicki Minaj as Donald Trump's new press secretary?
item.description: Rapper Nicki Minaj appeared with Trump at a recent rally in Michigan, where he made a comment about her “beautiful” and “hard to miss” butt. Now there's even talk of a possible job at the White House for the MAGA-loving rapper.

item.title: Cross-border network helps EU workers abroad claim wages and benefits
item.description: A cross-border network of counsellors, funded by the EU, is helping Europeans who work in other member states to claim the wages and social rights they are entitled to.

item.title: High-speed train crash in Spain kills at least 10 people, death toll expected to rise
item.description: The collision occured in central Spanish province of Toledo, south of Madrid. Rail service is now suspended between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia.

item.title: "Dead Poets Society" sells out eight consecutive months at Teatro da Trindade
item.description: The stage version of the film that captivated generations is sold out at Teatro da Trindade until the end of the year, before touring nationwide.

item.title: Mao meme comments won't 'cause serious economic problems' for Mbappé, says expert
item.description: Sports journalist Ken Early said Kylian Mbappé was probably “as surprised as anybody” after a joke involving a meme depicting the Real Madrid forward as Mao Zedong sparked a reaction by China.

item.title: French Senate backs bill making protesters pay up to €10,000 for unrest damage
item.description: Under the proposed law, which would also have to pass in the National Assembly, protesters could be required to pay up to €10,000 for damage caused during demonstrations.

item.title: Ex-Israel government spokesperson: 'Extraordinary comeback' by Netanyahu
item.description: Despite the fallout from the 7 October attacks, three years of war and widespread public dissatisfaction, Benjamin Netanyahu emerged from Israel's election with his political position strengthened, even as neither political bloc is assured of a parliamentary majority.

item.title: Brazil: Lula celebrates 81st birthday after re-election victory
item.description: Brazil's re-elected President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva celebrated his 81st birthday on Tuesday, 27 October, with dozens of supporters outside the Alvorada presidential palace in Brasília, just two days after winning a closely contested election.

item.title: 'Nail-biting' midterms may deliver Democratic wins across the US, says top Democratic strategist
item.description: Democratic party strategist Keith Brannum calls the upcoming US mid-term elections "far more nail-biting" than Republicans would have wanted, with many more potential wins for Democratic candidates than expected when first moving into 2026.

item.title: Serbian elections winner 'clearly seek better relations' with the EU, says expert
item.description: Marko Prelec, analyst at the International Crisis Group, believes dismantling outgoing prime minister Aleksandar Vučić system will take a long time but thinks it's "premature" to worry about the Students List movement capacity to lead the country.

item.title: German chemicals giant BASF raises profit guidance after Iran war price hikes
item.description: German chemicals giant BASF raised its 2026 outlook for the second time this year on Wednesday after raising prices for some products following the outbreak of the Iran war.

item.title: Ukraine: massive fire engulfs buildings after Russian strike on Kharkiv
item.description: Five people, including a 4-year-old child, were injured in an overnight Russian drone strike on Kharkiv. The attack set several buildings ablaze, with firefighters working under the threat of further strikes.

item.title: Israel votes in a pivotal election but no clear winner emerges
item.description: Good morning. It’s Wednesday and my name is Angela Skujins. In today’s newsletter: A new yet unclear era of Israeli politics, saying “do widzenia” to a Polish ambassador, and why energy is the chink in Europe’s defence armour. Let’s go.

item.title: Divers explore oldest medieval warship found off Sweden
item.description: Divers are investigating a remarkably well-preserved 15th-century shipwreck in Sweden's Stockholm archipelago.

item.title: EU Inc: Is the EU’s flagship start-up plan really dying over workers’ rights?
item.description: The EU’s 28th regime, the plan to help start-ups grow, has stalled in the European Parliament as political parties and trade unions warn it will deregulate workers’ rights. Watch the video!

item.title: Serbian police kill attacker outside Israeli Embassy in suspected ‘terrorist attack’
item.description: A similar attack took place outside the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade in June 2024, when a man wounded a Serbian police officer before being shot dead by a guard.

item.title: Travellers are making more sustainable choices to ‘enhance’ journeys, new study finds
item.description: Sustainability is playing a larger role in how and where we travel, with a new study revealing that exploring the outdoors, scenic rail journeys and visiting lesser-known destinations can enhance experiences abroad.

item.title: Europe Today: Israel faces deadlock after vote, Nordic leaders hold rare Putin call
item.description: Israel's election has ended in apparent deadlock, with neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor Gadi Eisenkot on track for a majority. Finland's and Norway's leaders have phoned Vladimir Putin as Europe seeks a seat at the table. We also cover Serbia's vote, the upcoming US midterms, and Mbappé's China row.

item.title: South Africa tests 7.6-kilometre freight train in bid to break world record
item.description: South Africa's state-owned logistics company Transnet says it has tested the world's longest freight train. Measuring 7.6 kilometres and made up of 696 empty wagons, the train travelled 860 kilometres from Saldanha Bay to an inland iron ore mine.

item.title: Ithaca's natural horseshoe harbour is picturesque – but it hides a dirty secret
item.description: Volunteer divers have removed almost 73 tonnes of solid waste from Greek seabeds across 13 years.

item.title: Zoom in, zoom out: Deeply personal and political pictures dominate Hungarian press photo exhibition
item.description: Political upheaval dominated the Hungarian Press Photo exhibition in 2025. Personal stories on how life is affected by tragedy and new technology such as AI, are at the heart of this year's competition entrants.

item.title: Trucker strikes emptied my local supermarket shelves: Shopping locally made all the difference
item.description: I didn’t think a trucker strike would really affect me - until supermarkets and petrol pumps were empty.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 28th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 28th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: After months dithering, Europe shows it's ready for talks with Russia
item.description: As Trump sides with Putin, Europeans are increasingly ready to engage in direct talks with Russia, something they have so far refused to do.

item.title: Cost of living crisis: How much net income do you need to live comfortably in Europe?
item.description: Living comfortably means different things to different people. Euronews Business calculated the monthly net household income needed to reach 150% of the national median which is the starting point of the upper-middle class benchmark.

item.title: Tech stocks soar as SK hynix adds to rising AI confidence
item.description: Asian tech stocks surged on blockbuster SK hynix earnings and renewed AI optimism, while investors weighed Israel’s election results and awaited key US tech earnings and the Federal Reserve’s policy decision.

item.title: Inside Ukraine's extraordinary underground pipeline operation against Russian forces near Kupiansk
item.description: Turning a tactic previously used by Russian troops against them, Ukrainian forces infiltrated enemy positions near Kupiansk in a carefully planned operation that inflicted significant losses and strengthened Kyiv's position in the area.

item.title: The pact that aims to return tourism's wealth to residents
item.description: A movement born in Malta wants to change tourism rules by involving hotels in local community life, returning visitors' wealth to residents and curbing gentrification.

item.title: Boeing shares tumble after it releases cautious growth forecast
item.description: Investors monitor Boeing shares after a slump on Tuesday weighed on sentiment following an update from the group on its outlook.

item.title: India evacuates tens of thousands as Cyclone Arnab makes landfall
item.description: Cyclone Arnab strengthened into a “very severe” cyclonic storm late Tuesday with gusting winds and heavy rain reported in several coastal areas.

item.title: Climate change should be declared health emergency as health risks can no longer be ignored
item.description: Climate change should be declared a global health emergency as its impacts intensify faster than action to address them, authors of a major new report warn.

item.title: What do Hispanic voters think about the US midterms?
item.description: Hispanic voters in South Texas who backed Donald Trump in 2024 are voicing frustration over the economy, immigration and the cost of living ahead of the US midterm elections.

item.title: Israel: opposition supporters celebrate narrow lead in exit polls
item.description: Supporters of Gadi Eisenkot celebrated in Tel Aviv as exit polls gave Israel's opposition bloc a narrow lead over Benjamin Netanyahu's camp, but no outright parliamentary majority.

item.title: Portugal: Lisbon housing crisis sparks protest outside parliament
item.description: Demonstrators gathered outside Portugal's parliament to protest against the housing crisis and police violence during recent camp clearances. The president has called for dialogue while defending police actions.

item.title: Israel election: Netanyahu bloc leads with more than half of votes counted but short of majority
item.description: The partial results are likely to change, and several exit polls showed the camps neck-and-neck without a majority.

item.title: Egypt’s parliament approves military support for Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks
item.description: Egypt has approved military help for Saudi Arabia if requested as Houthi attacks threaten the kingdom and Red Sea shipping. The vote comes as Saudi officials hold talks in Iran amid regional efforts to prevent a further escalation of the fighting.

item.title: Iraq sentences seven French nationals to prison for belonging to Islamic State
item.description: The men were deemed "particularly dangerous because of their role in threatening Iraq's national security, destabilising Iraq and Syria, and their involvement in inciting terrorist operations in other countries," a court statement said.

item.title: Norway says 'successful' cyberattacks against the country have tripled in last six months
item.description: The country's National Security Authority said the rapid growth of artificial intelligence technology also posed a "serious risk" to Norwegian businesses and organisations.

item.title: Qatar urges Iran to 'show goodwill' by ending threats to the region and reopening the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Regional powers are seeking a way out of the Iran war as attacks threaten shipping and energy supplies. Qatar says mediation continues after a visit to Tehran, where Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey have also held talks with Iranian leaders.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 27th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 27th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: South Africa: Athlete traverses 600 monkey bars under a 216-metre bridge
item.description: Suspended beneath South Africa's 216-metre-high Bloukrans Bridge, Thomas van Tonder crossed 600 monkey bars over more than 280 metres, completing the challenge in 47 minutes and 37 seconds.

item.title: Putin call pits Finland and Norway against Denmark and Sweden
item.description: Nordic unity broke on Tuesday after the leaders of Finland and Norway held a 90-minute phone call with Vladimir Putin. The Danish and Swedish prime ministers publicly cast doubt on the diplomatic overture.

item.title: European disease control center sends experts to Nigeria while Ebola cases surpass 10,000 in Congo
item.description: The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) deployed a team of experts to Nigeria this week as Ebola spreads across Africa, with cases reported in Kenya and Nigeria, the European agency announced on Tuesday.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro reportedly leaves Brazil for US after election defeat
item.description: A police source told the AFP news agency that Bolsonaro's passports had been "cancelled" and that there was "no formal record" of him leaving the country.

item.title: ‘Profiteering from pain’: Investments of super-rich fuel climate crisis and capitalise on recovery
item.description: Climate pledges fall short as Oxfam exposes how the super-rich profit from disaster.

item.title: Myanmar: spectacular lantern festival lights up ancient temples in Bagan
item.description: Hundreds of glowing lanterns floated into the night sky above Bagan's ancient pagodas. Thousands gathered to celebrate Thadingyut, Myanmar's Festival of Lights marking the end of Buddhist Lent.

item.title: Von der Leyen’s Canada ‘associate membership’ spurs battle of words with EU capitals
item.description: Germany, Italy, France and Greece objected to a draft EU-Canada declaration that cites von der Leyen’s ‘associate membership’ offer, as the member states fear legal uncertainty and a precedent for other third countries ahead of the Montreal summit on Thursday and Friday.

item.title: Two men charged over RAF Fairford air base incident, with one accused of assisting foreign intelligence
item.description: One of those charged, Mohmed Ahmad Abdulkarim, 24, has been accused of assisting a foreign intelligence service, which police believe to be Iran's.

item.title: Norwegian media sue Meta over plans to use their journalism for AI
item.description: Publishers say new terms for Facebook and Instagram business accounts could allow Meta to collect articles, images and videos from their websites without permission.
